questions.q: Who is recognized as the first recorded architect in history, responsible for the design of the Step Pyramid of Zoser?
questions.n: Imhotep was the vizier to Pharaoh Djoser and is credited with the revolutionary transition from mastaba to step pyramid.

questions.q: Which structure is considered the oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza pyramid complex?
questions.n: It is the largest pyramid in Giza and the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely intact.

questions.q: What is the term for the monumental gateway to an Egyptian temple, consisting of two sloped towers?
questions.n: The pylon represented the horizon between which the sun rose, serving as the formal entrance to the temple complex.

questions.q: In an Egyptian temple, what do you call the large hall filled with columns that support a flat roof?
questions.n: Hypostyle halls used massive, closely spaced columns to support heavy stone roofing slabs, as seen at Karnak.

questions.q: What are the monolithic stone pillars, usually square in plan with a pyramidal top, used as solar symbols?
questions.n: Obelisks were dedicated to the sun god Ra and were often tipped with electrum to catch the sun's rays.

questions.q: What is the masterpiece of Byzantine architecture, built by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidorus of Miletus?
questions.n: It was the largest cathedral in the world for nearly a thousand years and is famous for its massive dome.

questions.q: What structural element allows a circular dome to be placed over a square or rectangular plan?
questions.n: Pendentives are triangular segments of a sphere that transition the weight of the dome to four massive pillars.

questions.q: Which church in Ravenna is famous for its octagonal plan and exquisite mosaics of Emperor Justinian?
questions.n: San Vitale is a prime example of a Byzantine centrally planned church, known for its lavish mosaics.

questions.q: What is the term for the screen decorated with icons that separates the sanctuary from the nave in Byzantine churches?
questions.n: The iconostasis is a defining feature of Eastern Orthodox churches, holding multiple tiers of sacred images.

questions.q: What is the 'Curved' form of Byzantine capitals that often featured intricate 'basket' weaving or drill-work?
questions.n: Byzantine impost capitals used deep drill-work to create 'lace-like' patterns and often included an impost block on top.

questions.q: Who designed the iconic elliptical piazza and the massive colonnades leading to St. Peter’s Basilica?
questions.n: Bernini’s design for the piazza used two semicircular colonnades to represent the 'motherly arms of the church' embracing the faithful.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Church of San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane, famous for its undulating façade?
questions.n: Borromini was a master of complex curves and geometric ingenuity, creating a 'pulsating' architectural movement.

questions.q: What is the name of the grand palace in France that epitomizes the 'Baroque' style of power and absolute monarchy?
questions.n: Versailles transformed from a hunting lodge into a sprawling monument to Louis XIV's power and the French Baroque style.

questions.q: What do you call the 'Twisted' columns frequently used in Baroque altarpieces, notably in the St. Peter’s Baldachin?
questions.n: Named after the columns in the Temple of Solomon, their spiraling shafts emphasize Baroque movement and drama.

questions.q: What is the term for the technique using light and shadow to create a sense of three-dimensional depth and drama?
questions.n: Baroque artists and architects used bold contrasts of light and dark to emphasize volume and create theatrical effects.

questions.q: Who designed the Manila Cathedral (Post-war reconstruction) and the Philam Life Building on United Nations Avenue?
questions.n: Ocampo was responsible for the 8th reconstruction of the Manila Cathedral, blending Neo-Romanesque and Byzantine styles.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Meralco Building in Ortigas, recognized as the first 'curved' skyscraper in the Philippines?
questions.n: Zaragoza was a National Artist known for modern ecclesiastical and commercial designs, including this convex-faced building.

questions.q: The Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP), often described as a 'floating volume,' was designed by whom?
questions.n: Locsin's design uses massive cantilevered concrete blocks to create the illusion of a heavy volume floating over the ground.

questions.q: Who was the first Filipino architect to be named a National Artist for Architecture?
questions.n: Nakpil received the honor in 1973 for his contribution to modernizing Philippine architecture while respecting tradition.

questions.q: Which architect is known for the Tahanang Pilipino (Coconut Palace) and pioneered the use of indigenous materials?
questions.n: Mañosa championed the idea that 'Philippine architecture must be Filipino,' using wood, rattan, and capiz.

questions.q: In a Bahay na Bato, what is the name of the elevated porch or open terrace used for washing and drying?
questions.n: Located at the back of the house, the azotea served utilitarian needs and as a garden space.

questions.q: What is the 'overhanging' second floor of the Bahay na Bato called, which provides shade to the ground floor?
questions.n: The volada is a cantilevered gallery that allows the family to move around the house without going through private rooms.

questions.q: What do you call the ornate wooden carvings or latticework found above doors and partitions to allow air circulation?
questions.n: Callado panels are decorative and functional, ensuring cross-ventilation in the tropical climate.

questions.q: Under RA 10066 (National Cultural Heritage Act), what is the term for a cultural property with exceptional cultural, artistic, and historical significance?
questions.n: This is the highest designation for cultural property in the Philippines, granted by the government.

questions.q: Which Filipino church is the only one in the country built entirely of steel?
questions.n: It is a Neo-Gothic church with steel parts prefabricated in Belgium and assembled in Manila.
